audit_findings.title: Core client-float interest appears to have been removed from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $67m FY2025 pretax interest-income pool, equal to 60.4% of the $110.9m anchor; client-float portion unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Retaining the after-tax client-float interest increases anchor OE and every projected cash flow; only interest attributable to corporate cash added in the bridge should be purged.
audit_findings.evidence: We recognize interest income on cash and investments as revenue because the collection and processing of funds held for the benefit of our clients are critical components of providing these services and the associated interest we earn is a core part of our operations.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated methodological mismatch: the filing classifies interest earned through collecting and processing client funds as core operating revenue, while the valuation states that portfolio interest was purged. The exact error remains unresolved because the $67m also includes corporate-cash and tax-refund interest. Given the interest pool's scale relative to anchor OE, the client-float portion is reasonably capable of materially increasing value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile FY2025 interest income by source, retain the after-tax amount earned on client, WSE and TriNet Trust funds, purge only interest associated with the $358m bridge cash, and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The full cash bridge may include cash required inside the business
audit_findings.magnitude: $358m bridge addition, or $7.25 per diluted share and 18.7% of $1,916m base equity value; required reserve unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any cash required for operations, regulation, insurance support or minimum liquidity must remain in the business and should be removed from the excess-cash equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: We use our available cash and cash equivalents to satisfy our operational and regulatory requirements and to fund capital expenditures.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved possibility rather than a demonstrated error: the filing identifies $352m of June 2026 corporate cash, but it does not establish how much is distributable. The maximum affected bridge amount is large; excluding the full $358m would reduce base value from $38.83 to approximately $31.58 per share and the buy-below level from $27.18 to approximately $22.10.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $358m bridge to June 2026 corporate cash categories, document minimum operating and regulatory liquidity using historical cash needs and contractual requirements, and rerun the bridge using only evidenced excess cash.

audit_findings.title: Rejected payroll-tax credits could create an unrecoverable common-equity loss
audit_findings.magnitude: $310m ERTC receivable at June 2026, including $21m net already distributed to clients; penalties, collection losses and reserves unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Rejected credits can create repayment, penalty or interest obligations; losses not recoverable from clients would reduce OE or require a direct deduction from equity value.
audit_findings.evidence: While our clients are contractually responsible to us for their errors in tax credit submissions and for repaying us for all rejected tax credits under our service contracts, taxing authorities may still look to TriNet for repayment and we may not be able to effectively enforce or collect on these obligations.
audit_findings.explanation: The exposure mechanism and ongoing IRS examinations are demonstrated, but no rejection, inadequate reserve or collection loss is established. Most of the $310m receivable has a corresponding client liability, so it is not itself a $310m equity exposure. The identified $21m already distributed equals about $0.43 per diluted share and 1.1% of base equity value, which alone is not conclusion-changing, but additional penalties and unrecoverable client claims are unquantified.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the claim-level ERTC roll-forward, IRS examination status, corresponding client liabilities, the $21m distribution aging, client credit assessments, reimbursement enforcement history, and reserves; rerun for evidenced expected loss and penalties.

audit_findings.title: The 2025 earnings anchor includes favorable prior-year insurance reserve development
audit_findings.magnitude: $13m FY2025 pretax favorable development; approximately $9.23m after 29% tax, 8.3% of anchor OE, implying about $130m or $2.63 per share of base value if fully removed
audit_findings.mechanism: A reserve release increases the anchor OE; treating it as recurring propagates the benefit through forecast OE and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: For the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, the favorable development is due to lower than expected reported claim frequency and severity for the more recent years.
audit_findings.explanation: The $13m favorable prior-year development is demonstrated and material relative to the $110.9m anchor. What remains unresolved is whether repeated favorable development represents sustainable underwriting economics or nonrecurring estimate revision. A neutral-development rerun could reduce base value by roughly 6.8%, so the treatment is material even though it would not eliminate the existing gap between market price and modeled value.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the $13m is retained in anchor OE, analyze at least five years of favorable and adverse development, and rerun neutral-development and filed adverse-sensitivity cases without changing other inputs.

audit_findings.title: Temporary restructuring expense may have been capitalized as a perpetual operating burden
audit_findings.magnitude: $11m FY2025 restructuring expense and $13m in the first half of 2026; normalized recurring component unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Leaving a temporary charge in anchor OE understates all forecast cash flows and terminal value, while removing it immediately overstates near-term OE because restructuring continued in 2026.
audit_findings.evidence: We expect the restructuring efforts to continue through 2026 and may recognize additional expenses as they are incurred.
audit_findings.explanation: The charges and their continuation through 2026 are demonstrated, but their remaining duration and genuinely recurring transformation cost are unresolved. The FY2025 charge equals 9.9% of anchor OE; a full after-tax removal at the 29% FY2025 rate would add about $7.81m to anchor OE and approximately $110m, or $2.22 per share, to base value. The filed $13m first-half 2026 charge shows that a simple immediate add-back would also be inappropriate.
audit_findings.action: Trace restructuring treatment in the $110.9m anchor, obtain the remaining 2026 cash-cost forecast and expected savings, then rerun with explicit finite transition costs followed by a normalized recurring expense base.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $38.0m FY2022 residual, equal to 9.3% of FY2022 OE; current-anchor residual and eligible portion unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any residual D&A proven to represent eligible non-economic amortization would be added back to OE, increasing forecast cash flows and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2022 $38.0m (37.6% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: There is no demonstrated overvaluation because unidentified D&A was retained as an expense. The FY2022 residual is filed/computed and conservatively lowers that year's OE, but the record does not identify the corresponding FY2025 amount or establish that any residual qualifies for an add-back. Materiality to the current anchor therefore cannot be determined.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile FY2025 filed D&A by depreciation, acquired-intangible amortization, internally developed software amortization and other components; add back only amounts supported as non-economic and rerun if the eligible amount is significant.
